readings.title: 科学的方法

readings.title: 学习一门语言
readings.text: A bilingual mind starts with vocabulary and one careful utterance at a time. We encode meaning and let a teacher facilitate our progress as we interact with real talk. Be explicit about your aim and stay evident in what you mean; build conceptual links between the new language and your own. A cognitive habit of ten minutes a day beats one long lesson. Use linguistic and semantic clues, keep your grammatical accuracy honest, and welcome each adaptation to a new sound. My mother learns with a book; my father listens on the bus. At school a student should speak more and fear less. A friend and I cook food from another culture and name each thing in the new words. We write notes in the morning and read them again at night. A language is not a test; it is a door to people, to stories, and to a wider home in the world. We speak each day and listen with care; a good book and a small step help us learn a new language and meet kind people.
